facts.claim: "Rage" by Medium Build was released as a single on September 14, 2022, and runs 2:41.
Shazam and Discogs credit the writing to Nicholas Carpenter (Medium Build) and Jake LiBassi, and the production to Laiko. Other sources list Carpenter alone as writer.
Discogs lists Laiko as producer and Jake LiBassi as writer of "Rage", with mixing by Jimmy Mansfield and mastering by Adam Grover.
Shazam's credits list Medium Build and Laiko on programming. Jimmy Mansfield is credited as mixing engineer and Adam Grover as mastering engineer.
"Rage" was later included as the closing track on Medium Build's EP Health, released January 25, 2023 on Island Records.
The lyrics are about an inner rage, regret and fear of losing a loved one's affection, along with a wish to be held and called by his real name.
Medium Build is the project of Nick (Nicholas) Carpenter. He joined Island Records in partnership with slowplay in 2023 and released the Health EP.
Carpenter launched Medium Build in 2015. He studied music at Middle Tennessee State University and later moved to Anchorage, Alaska.
Carpenter says he created Medium Build as a safe place for his intrusive thoughts. He says the persona eventually merged with his real self.
Medium Build's Bandcamp tags him as Alaska, alternative pop, indie pop and Anchorage.

research.lineage: Medium Build is an Alaska-based, Atlanta-born alternative/indie pop songwriter whose confessional, genre-blending style draws on folk, pop and hip-hop influences.

draft:
The word **"Rage"** never gets shouted. Medium Build sings it in a breathy, slightly nasal voice with a little vibrato on the held notes, over clean electric guitar arpeggios and a slow beat that drags its feet. Nothing in the music boils over. That gap between the title and the sound is the song.

What the lyrics describe isn't an outburst. It's an admission made by someone who wants to be held. The opening lines ask to be kissed, held, and squeezed close. The narrator says they've spent a long time trying to act tough, and then comes the request that cuts deepest: "Say my real name." This person has been living as some armored version of themselves, and the plea is to be seen past it. Carpenter has said he started Medium Build as a safe place for his intrusive thoughts, and that the persona eventually merged with who he really is. The song doesn't explain the line, but those two ideas sit close together.

The chorus repeats one confession, the rage inside, and adds nothing to it. No reason, no target, no apology. The apology arrives later, in the verse where the song stops circling: "I get scared, I get mean." Five plain words connect fear to cruelty, which is the most honest thing a person in a fight can say and the hardest to say out loud. Right before that comes regret buried in the chest, and right after it a request not to take the love away. The narrator doesn't ask to be let off. They ask to be called out, "Please don't give up on me now," which means asking for accountability and patience at once. Shame and need sit side by side, and the song leaves them there.

The band plays like it's trying not to startle anyone. The bass holds simple root notes. The drums keep a steady kick, snare, and hi-hat. The guitar picks through its chords in that clean, reverb-washed way indie pop uses to suggest an empty room late at night. The production is polished and roomy, and the voice stands alone with no harmonies to soften it. Carpenter co-wrote it with Jake LiBassi, Laiko produced, and the song later closed Medium Build's *Health* EP on Island. That's a fitting place for it: an ending that is really a request to stay.

The song lets you feel how anger can be the loudest form of being afraid you'll be left, and it makes the quiet version of that fear sound like the true one.
